content.summary: Reviewed stage invalidation, counted semantic repairs and conditional derived-fact comparison. The comparison evaluates a declared finite common domain, maps snapshots explicitly, and runs both original generated Java classes in batches.
findings: Dependency and extraction failures cannot be repaired by another rule-generation prompt.
Repair reservation precedes dispatch, identical evidence cannot trigger a repeat and failed reservations count.
Output polarity normalizes only known Booleans; UNKNOWN, CONFLICT and OUT_OF_SCOPE survive.
Derived mappings bind source and candidate hashes and all fact bindings; date/numeric domains must be explicitly supplied.
Exhaustive declared-domain comparisons are conditional on mapping assumptions and do not grant authority.
Java witness checks use originals, not only a rewritten normalized program.
